title: Parity anomaly governs the thermal Hall response of chiral superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene above and below $T_c$
summary: Chiral superconductivity has recently been confirmed in rhombohedral tetra- and pentalayer graphene near the BCS--BEC crossover, but no theory tells the experimentalist what thermal Hall response to expect, or why any signal should persist above the phase-coherence temperature $T_c$. We show that the parity anomaly of $(2{+}1)$-dimensional field theory fixes the answer exactly, at all temperatures, with no free parameters: $κ_{xy}/T = (π^2 k_B^2/6h)\,C_{\rm BdG}\,\tanh[Δ(T)/(2k_BT)]$, where $C_{\rm BdG}$ is the BdG Chern number and $Δ(T)$ is the fermionic excitation gap.
